intake: The fundamental-rights impact assessment starts as a structured intake questionnaire — data, not a Word document — covering intended use and context of deployment.
dpia: The GDPR Art. 35 data-protection impact assessment, cross-referenced so shared elements are written once and the two assessments do not drift apart.
assessment: A rights-risk assessment over the affected groups and the risks to their rights, re-opened when the system changes rather than described at a single moment.
mitigations: For each identified risk, a mitigation linked to the control that implements it — a Policy Card, an Eval Gate or a runtime guardrail.
gate: The single approval gate where a named reviewer signs off on the residual risk before a high-risk system is deployed under EU AI Act Art. 27.
reviewer: The human reviewer — DPO, legal or compliance — accountable for the sign-off at the gate.
record: The machine-readable FRIA record produced by the sign-off, versioned and stored with the registry entry where the auditor looks.
